Only a single assertion checks one property (the integer returned). There are not multiple assertions verifying different properties of the result, making detection of deeper faults less likely.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present in the provided snippet. Tests appear active and runnable.
No annotations or comments reference requirement IDs, tickets, or user stories; the class-level Javadoc does not include requirement identifiers, so traceability is absent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: No performance or security tests are expected in this small unit test; no timeout-based profiling or security assertions are present. Per rules, this is typically not-applicable for such unit tests.
Method name 'test7' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions that indicate scenario and expected result; does not communicate purpose.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: Presence of EvoSuite runner imports, EvoRunnerParameters, and an auto-generated style test name (test7) suggests the test was generated and retains auto-generated characteristics, indicating heavy code-generation artifacts.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: No Given-When-Then structure or BDD-style naming is present in the method; the class contains only a minimal happy-path test which suggests tests were not comprehensively designed/prioritized.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (constructor and numVertices) and does not use reflection or access internals; it verifies observable behavior rather than implementation details.
Assertions lack descriptive failure messages and there is only one assertion; the test would benefit from specific assertion messages to aid diagnosis.
Class-level Javadoc describes the purpose and improvements; there are no excessive inline comments or commented-out code. Comments present add value rather than clutter.
No sources of non-determinism (no Random, time-based calls, Thread.sleep, or external resources) are present in the test method; behavior is deterministic given same inputs.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only creates in-memory objects and doesn't persist data, modify static fields, or open external resources; no cleanup is required in this snippet.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: Class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing categorization for selective execution; labeling is present at class level.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one clear Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root-cause identification easier. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if the test has exactly one Act (method under test) and one assertion group. DECISION RULES: 1) Count Act operations. The method calls grafo0.insereAresta(...) and grafo0.retiraAresta(...): >1 distinct Acts -> non-compliant. 2) Test name doesn't indicate multiple operations but presence of two operations is sufficient. 3) Not a single method-call-and-assert case. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test performs multiple operations (insert and remove) in one test, violating atomicity.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on each other and should use setup/teardown. RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary execution order. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use @Before/@After or only local variables. DECISION RULES: No @Before/@After found, but the test uses only local variables and does not modify shared/static state; therefore compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test uses only local state and has no inter-test dependencies.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: For each method under test provide at least a happy path and an error scenario. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness and exception handling. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if class contains at least two test methods covering happy and error cases (or use of assertThrows/@Test(expected=...)). DECISION RULES: The class has only one test method (test6) and it exercises a single, likely happy-path-like scenario; no exception or invalid-input test is present -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant due to absence of a second test covering exceptional/error flows.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary inputs (0, negative, max, empty). RATIONALE: Boundaries often reveal off-by-one errors. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test uses values like 0, -1, MAX_VALUE, empty strings. DECISION RULES: The test uses 0 as an index (grafo0.insereAresta(0,...)), which is a boundary value; therefore it leans compliant. VERDICT: compliant because the test includes the boundary value 0.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and modular; reuse helpers for repeated logic. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if helper methods or constants are used OR if tests are short and not duplicative. DECISION RULES: No helper methods are found, but the single test is short (<10 lines) and does not duplicate code across methods. VERDICT: compliant (small, self-contained test with no evident duplication).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and avoid loops/complex conditionals. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to maintain and less error-prone. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if <20 lines, no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: The test is short (~6 lines) with linear flow and no loops or branches. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive and verify multiple properties. RATIONALE: Multiple property checks increase fault detection. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if test verifies >=2 properties of result (e.g., various fields or size+contents). DECISION RULES: The test contains two assertions (assertNull on removed edge and assertEquals on numVertices), verifying multiple properties. VERDICT: compliant because it asserts two distinct aspects of system state.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or commented-out tests; keep tests active. RATIONALE: Ignored tests can hide regressions. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: No @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests are present; the method is active. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be linked to requirement IDs or stories. RATIONALE: Traceability helps map tests to requirements. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if annotations or Javadoc reference REQ-/US-/JIRA- ids. DECISION RULES: No @Story/@Requirement/@Issue annotations or Javadoc containing requirement IDs are present. Only a generic class Javadoc exists that does not reference a requirement. VERDICT: non-compliant due to absence of traceability metadata.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance and security should be tested separately. RATIONALE: Non-functional tests are separate concerns. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Mark not-applicable for typical unit tests unless explicit timing or security tests are present. DECISION RULES: This is a small unit test with a timeout but no explicit performance/security assertions; practice is usually not applicable for standard unit tests. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Names help understand failures. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if name follows methodName_scenario_expectedResult or similar. DECISION RULES: The method is named 'test6' which is generic and does not communicate intent -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant due to non-descriptive test name.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid verbose autogenerated tests and names like test0/test1. RATIONALE: Auto-generated code is often verbose and hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no signs of generation; non-compliant if auto-generated patterns or names exist. DECISION RULES: The class uses EvoSuite runner annotations and the method name 'test6' suggests generated tests (and the class comment indicates it was improved from EvoSuite). These are signals of code-generation origin -> non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant due to generator artifacts (EvoRunner usage and test6 name).

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then or BDD naming) and be prioritized. RATIONALE: Thoughtful design yields more comprehensive tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming are present or coverage includes multiple scenarios. DECISION RULES: The class contains a single minimal test (happy path-like) without Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming; therefore non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because there is no clear evidence of test-first or prioritized design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should rely on public APIs and avoid internal implementation details. RATIONALE: Behavior-focused tests are less brittle. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests call only public methods and don't use reflection. DECISION RULES: The test uses public constructor and public methods (insereAresta, retiraAresta, numVertices) and uses no reflection or private-field access -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and include descriptive messages when helpful. RATIONALE: Clear assertions make failures easier to diagnose. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if >=50% assertions include messages or use specific assertions rather than generic ones. DECISION RULES: The test uses two assertions but none include descriptive messages; while they are specific (assertNull/assertEquals), the guidance expects messages or descriptive assertions. With 0 assertions containing messages (<50%), mark as non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because assertions lack descriptive failure messages.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain why, not what; avoid excessive comments or commented-out code. RATIONALE: Clear, limited comments aid maintenance. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no commented-out code and comments (if any) are minimal and useful. DECISION RULES: No commented-out code present and class-level Javadoc is concise; thus compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid non-determinism (randomness, time, sleeps, external deps). RATIONALE: Deterministic tests prevent flakiness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if no Random/System.currentTimeMillis/Thread.sleep or external dependency usage without mocking. DECISION RULES: No such non-deterministic constructs are present. The test uses only deterministic constructor and method calls -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not leave persistent side effects or modify shared state. RATIONALE: Side-effect-free tests can run in any order. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if tests use local variables and do not persist data or modify static variables. DECISION RULES: This test uses only local variables and does not create files or global state; no cleanup required -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories to organize tests (e.g., @Tag, @Category). RATIONALE: Enables selective execution and classification. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if @Tag/@Category/@Category usage present. DECISION RULES: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) and a UnitTest interface is defined; therefore the test is categorized -> compliant. VERDICT: compliant.
